Chartering a Private Dahabiya: Cost, Cabins and How It Works

How a private dahabiya charter works: the whole boat for your party, cabins, crew and food, the Esna to Aswan route, cost and how far ahead to book

15 November 2026 · 11 minute read

By Islam Hussein, Sillage Égypte journey designer. Last updated: November 2026.

The quick answer

A private dahabiya charter reserves the whole boat for one party. We publish no whole-boat price: on a Sillage journey the river sits inside a per-person journey price. The Complete Egypt, 13 days with five dahabiya nights from Esna to Aswan, starts from €7,500 per person for two or more travellers. Dahabiyas typically have 8 to 12 cabins, air-conditioned and en suite. In our experience, book nine to twelve months ahead for Christmas and New Year, and three to six months for most of the rest of the year.

Some travellers ask about Nile journeys. Others ask a simpler question: can we have the boat? This post is for the second kind. A private dahabiya charter, a shallow-draught wooden sailing boat with a limited number of cabins and a full crew, reserved for a single party, is the quietest way to travel the Nile, and its mechanics are more straightforward than the romance suggests. Sillage Égypte (sillage-egypte.com), the private Egypt journey designer, builds such charters into its journeys, and every journey is private throughout: your own car, your own certified Egyptologist from the first day to the last, no scheduled departures, no shared groups, and where a dahabiya belongs in it, the whole boat for one party. What follows is how a charter works, who fits aboard, the crew and the food, the route, the cost and the lead times.

The short answer

A private dahabiya charter buys the entire vessel: every cabin, the skipper and his sailors, the chef and the table he cooks for. A charter can be as small as two travellers, and on a Sillage journey you pay the journey's per-person price, not a bill for empty cabins.

One line each, before the detail:

  • A couple: a private house on water, with the crew working for two.
  • A family: one boat, one timetable, your children's bedtimes honoured rather than negotiated; from reading age upwards it works beautifully.
  • A group of friends: one long table, evenings with nothing scheduled and nothing missed.
  • Photographers and readers: you came for the light and the silence; both come with the hull.
  • If the question is really whether the river belongs in your journey at all: begin with our six journeys compared, then return here.

Costs are covered properly below, with a real journey to anchor them. First, the mechanics.

How a private dahabiya charter works

You get the boat, not a berth. A charter reserves the whole dahabiya (cabins, crew, galley and itinerary) for your party alone; no other guests join, and no departure exists until yours does. The steps are simple:

  1. You describe your party, your dates and your hopes to a journey designer. The enquiry is free and without obligation, and a real person replies within 24 hours.
  2. The designer matches a boat to you. The right boat for four guests in March is not necessarily the right one for fourteen in December, so it is chosen for your dates and named in your proposal.
  3. The river days are built into a private journey around them: nights aboard, the moorings, and the certified Egyptologist who travels with you from the first day to the last.
  4. A 25% non-refundable deposit secures the boat and the journey; the balance is due 60 days before arrival (a booking made inside 60 days is paid in full). The price is fixed once Sillage confirms in writing, except for government action, taxes and fees, or significant currency changes, and travel insurance is a condition of booking. The full position is in our booking terms.
  5. You travel. The crew handle the boat, the chef the table, your Egyptologist the walls, and the design team everything between.

Sailing, towing and the wind

A dahabiya genuinely sails: two masts, canvas, and silence whenever the northerly wind is doing its work. When the wind drops, a small motorboat tows the boat (Afar describes the same routine), and that is nothing to be scandalised by. The honest version is this: the boat keeps every promise of a sailing vessel except the one about sailing every hour, and in exchange it keeps a pace no engine can imitate.

Cabins and who fits

Dahabiyas typically have 8 to 12 cabins, air-conditioned and en suite, with no other party to share the decks. There is typically no pool, spa or gym; the river does that work. Party size is the first question in choosing a boat.

Your party What to expect The honest read
One Possible; priced in the proposal Ask, and we will tell you plainly what it means
Two The whole boat for two, at the journey's per-person price A private house on water
Four to ten The whole boat, with cabins to spare or close to full The charter's natural size: one table, one timetable
Over ten The larger boats; priced in the proposal Fewer boats to choose from, so start early

One warning worth writing down: the boats are not step-free. Gangplanks can be steep and companionways steeper. Travellers for whom stairs are the constraint are better served by a ship.

How many guests fit on a private dahabiya?

With typically 8 to 12 cabins, and two to a cabin, a full boat sleeps about 16 to 24 guests. Few parties fill one, and they do not need to: a couple can have a boat alone. A full boat of the largest size is closer to a small village than a party, and we would say so before you booked it.

Children count toward the berths, and toward the pleasure of the sandbanks, in equal measure. Beyond about twenty-four guests the honest answer is a ship.

Crew and food aboard

Expect a full crew: skipper, sailors, a chef, stewards. The chef cooks for your table alone, which is the entire point of the exercise, and on The Complete Egypt all meals are taken aboard during the river nights.

Food aboard is the Egyptian kitchen at family scale: mezzeh, lentil soup, and strong Egyptian tea whenever the boat goes quiet. Evenings are quiet, deliberately: dark water, an early bed, and the strange luxury of hearing the river work. Power on a dahabiya comes from a generator, and on some boats the main one is switched off overnight, so the boat keeps early hours. Boats differ on points like this, and it is why the boat is chosen for your dates and named in your proposal.

The route: Esna to Aswan

Most private charters run four to six nights on the Luxor to Aswan stretch of the river. On The Complete Egypt the river is five nights, boarding at Esna and sailing upstream to Aswan on the north wind. Nights are spent moored where the deep-draught ships cannot go: against the riverbank below the quarried cliffs of Gebel el-Silsila, or off the village fields of El-Kab, where the evening walk is a sandbank.

Notes on the river days:

  • Edfu's Temple of Horus is among the best-preserved temples in Egypt, and it is busiest in the middle of the day. Early on, it is much quieter.
  • Kom Ombo: the double temple of Sobek and Horus, set directly above the river.
  • At Gebel el-Silsila, look for the rock-cut shrines the pharaohs left in the quarry cliffs.
  • A journey can be shaped so that the Temple of Hathor at Dendera, north of Luxor, is reached from the river rather than by road. Ask your designer whether it fits your dates.

What a private dahabiya charter costs

We publish no whole-boat price. On a Sillage journey you pay a per-person journey price with the river nights inside it, and any solo traveller or larger party is priced in the proposal.

For scale, anchor the question to a real journey. The Complete Egypt is 13 days: Cairo, Luxor, five nights on a private dahabiya from Esna to Aswan, Abu Simbel by air, and the pyramids kept for the last day, with a certified Egyptologist throughout, private cars and luxury hotels. It starts from €7,500 per person for two or more travellers, with domestic flights and the visa included. Gratuities and international flights are not included. What the difference from a ship buys is not thread count; it is the moorings, the hours at the temples and the silence.

One honest note. The festive weeks price the river at its highest: Christmas & New Year on the Nile is a 14-day journey with six nights on a chartered dahabiya, from €9,999 per person, and Christmas, New Year and Easter carry a supplement on other journeys.

When to book

These are the lead times we find work, from experience rather than data: nine to twelve months for Christmas and New Year, six to nine for Easter, four to six for high winter, three to six for the shoulder months, and six to ten weeks for summer. There are only so many good boats, and the festive weeks take the best of them first. A 25% non-refundable deposit secures your dates, and the balance falls due 60 days before arrival. What the festive weeks look like on the water is covered in our Christmas and New Year in Egypt guide.

FAQ

Can I rent a whole dahabiya on the Nile? Yes. Dahabiyas are chartered whole, and on a Sillage journey the boat is reserved for one travelling party alone: every cabin, the crew and the chef. A party of two can have one. Some other operators sell individual cabins on shared departures; that is a different product, and a different price logic.

What does a night's charter cost? We publish no nightly boat price. The river sits inside the journey's per-person price: The Complete Egypt, 13 days including five nights aboard a private dahabiya, starts from €7,500 per person for two or more travellers. Solo travellers and larger parties are priced in the proposal.

How many people can sleep aboard? Dahabiyas typically have 8 to 12 cabins, so a full boat sleeps about 16 to 24 at two to a cabin. Most parties are far smaller; beyond about twenty-four, the honest answer is a ship.

Is a dahabiya good for a family or a group of friends? Both, and often ideally. A family gets one timetable and the children get the sandbanks; friends get a long table and unscheduled evenings. Families with children below reading age often prefer a ship, where the pool and the playmates are.

Will we actually sail? Under sail whenever the northerly wind serves; a small tow boat when it drops. Most voyages do some of each, and the day's shape belongs to the river rather than to a departure slot.

How far ahead must I book? In our experience, nine to twelve months for Christmas and New Year, six to nine for Easter, four to six for high winter, three to six for the shoulder months and six to ten weeks for summer. A 25% non-refundable deposit secures the dates once the proposal is right.

Can I book one cabin and share the boat with others? Not on a Sillage journey. Every journey is private throughout, with no shared departures and no scheduled groups, so where a dahabiya belongs in one, the whole boat is chartered for your party and chosen for your dates.

The takeaway

A private dahabiya charter is the whole boat for your party: typically 8 to 12 cabins, a full crew, and five nights of water between Esna and Aswan on The Complete Egypt, inside a per-person journey price from €7,500. It suits couples, families and groups of friends who count silence as an amenity. If that is your party, plan your journey; a named designer replies within 24 hours, and the right boat is easier to find if you start in time.
